newsitem.title: USA: Utilities band together in face of deregulation.
newsitem.headline: Utilities band together in face of deregulation.

text.p: Facing an uncertain future due to the deregulation of the $310 billion U.S. natural gas and electricity retail market, utilities are banding together to market their services.

On Monday, UtiliCorp United Inc and PECO Energy Co said that they will launch a service company franchise called EnergyOne which will offer consumers the opportunity to buy energy plus AT&T Corp's telephone and ADT Ltd home security products in one package.
They will franchise their services to other utilities and will charge them a fee of $10 million for a company with $2.0 billion in revenues.
At the same time, Suburban Propane Partners LP finalized a reciprocal marketing agreement with Duke Energy Corp to offer customers the one-stop shopping for propane and natural gas.
The UtiliCorp/PECO combination aims to franchise its services around the country and hopes to attract customers attracted by a package of discounts and the convenience of one-stop shopping.

"When the U.S. electricity industry is deregulated, the difference in prices between competing services will be very small, so competition will be on the convenience of service," said Dan Rudakas, analyst at EVEREN Securities.
UtiliCorp had previously tried to market branded electricity nationally under the EnergyOne name, but found the effort too expensive.
UtiliCorp's chief executive Richard Green told a press conference in Washington that utilities have to focus on the service side of the business, because that's where the margins are biggest.
"On the gas and electric commodity side of the business, there is a price war relationship with your customer with very slim margins," he said.
The venture expects to have six utilities and 10 million customers signed up by the end of the year and is looking for a third parner.
"Our research indicates that consumers have tired of dealing with multiple suppliers for what are repetitive, essential utility services," said Andrew Guariello, president and CEO of EnergyOne.
EVEREN's Rudakas anticipates that the EnergyOne service will be attractive both to both retail customers and the utilities which will buy its services.

"Every time you sit down to dinner you get a phonecall from AT&T or another operator trying to sell their phone services. When electricity is deregulated the same thing will happen, but so long as EnergyOne provides a decent service, customers are likely to stay with them," Rudakas said.
